notes: C8 failed as sealed, and is kept. The mock network already held a release of the living site's name by another key: names here are derived from a node's key but not bound to it, so the first to record a name holds it. The merge refused the living site's own release, as predicted, and, because the auditor's gate credits a value only to the key that gave the answer (written before the first run, as part of the gate), it also refused the ten values that would otherwise have been credited to the key that took the name: eleven refusals, not the one the claim expected, and the living site has no part in the network's allocation. The books are right to refuse; the lesson is to bind a node's name to its key before any merge.

C10 failed as sealed, and is kept. The page's own text carries none of the barred words. The sealed rule also holds the source of every module of core/phase6/ to the list, names in the code and test data included: page.mjs calls break-it's gated cost kernel by the name break-it gave its reader of a dated list of what services cost, and keeps that list in a variable named after it; the two test files use barred words as the data they test the barred-word check and the judge with. Nothing was renamed away after the measurement; each module's findings are in the facts (c10.modules).
